summary.oneLiner: NRB Industrial Bearings Limited (NIBL) manufactures needle roller and other precision bearings for industrial applications, with turnover of Rs. 7,562.01 lakhs in FY2025-26.
summary.business: The Company manufactures bearings for industrial applications, and states there has been no change in the main nature of its business during FY2025-26. It runs a manufacturing facility supported by a fully equipped Research & Development Centre that develops new products aligned to evolving customer requirements and enhances existing product lines. NIBL sells to domestic OEMs and distribution channels and exports, and holds 35% stakes in two associate companies, NRB-IBC Bearings Private Limited and NIBL-Korta Engineering Private Limited.

Industrial bearings: Needle roller and roller thrust bearings
Cam followers (including heavy series cam follower)
Races (including races for heavy duty ball bearing series)

currentContext.expansion: The annual report describes no named plant, line or capacity project with a commissioning or ramp timeline. Expansion is framed qualitatively: the Company states it continues to invest in its manufacturing facility, supported by a fully equipped Research & Development Centre whose team works on new product development aligned with evolving customer requirements and on enhancing existing product lines. In line with its expansion strategy NIBL is strengthening its distribution footprint in untapped markets, particularly Tier 2 cities across India, to reach emerging industrial clusters, and is expanding its presence in underpenetrated regions of India, Asia and the Americas, with new export markets such as the USA and South East Asian countries. A capital-commitments note is disclosed (estimated amount of contracts remaining to be executed on capital account and not provided for, net of advances of Rs. 200.28 lakhs; as at March 31, 2025: Rs. 37.22 lakhs), but the block supplied does not allow the commitment figure itself to be attributed to a period.

risks.risk: Import competition from Chinese machines and mechanical components, including bearings
risks.note: Management states the rapid growth of imports of Chinese machines and mechanical components including bearings is reshaping the market, and that rising adoption of imported Chinese harvester machines eroded market share for local manufacturers, impacting revenue from the agriculture segment.

risks.risk: Automotive bearing manufacturers pivoting into the industrial segment
risks.note: Complemented by the Government's initiative to promote the Electric Vehicle segment, several automotive bearing manufacturers began redirecting their focus toward the industrial sector, resulting in intensified competition and a more saturated market landscape - directly in NIBL's core industrial-bearing market.

risks.risk: Customer / OEM schedule concentration in weak end-segments
risks.note: A significant decline in schedules from key OEMs in the textile and Radial Piston Pump segments, along with reduced demand from textile end-users, affected revenue in those segments - showing dependence on a small set of OEM schedules.

risks.risk: End-market cyclicality and uneven segment performance
risks.note: While Industrial Gearboxes, Construction Machinery, Material Handling Equipment and Machine Tools performed in line with forecasts, Textile Machinery and Mining fell short of expectations; management notes market dynamics remain volatile and demand patterns continue to evolve.

The overall business environment remained challenging within the industrial segment due to global economic uncertainty, rising geopolitical tensions, and disruptions caused by inter-country conflicts and policy shifts.

The Company reports foreign exchange earnings of Rs. 2,300.31 lakhs and outgo of Rs. 586.79 lakhs for FY2025-26, and its growth mantra rests on entering new export markets such as the USA and South East Asian countries, so a material share of business is exposed to currency and cross-border trade conditions.

Cost efficiency in the year came from stringent cost control in raw material and finished goods inventory; the energy annexure shows propane gas cost rose to Rs. 1,78,400 per ton from Rs. 69,800, and solar generation fell to 1,31,473 KWh from 3,19,879 KWh, leaving more of the load on purchased power.

Based on paid-up equity share capital and net worth, the corporate governance provisions of SEBI LODR are not applicable to the Company; it provides a Corporate Governance report only on a voluntary basis. CSR provisions of Section 135 are likewise not applicable, and no CSR policy or activities exist.

risks.body:

- Complemented by the Government's initiative to promote the Electric Vehicle segment, several automotive bearing manufacturers began redirecting their focus toward the industrial sector, resulting in intensified competition and a more saturated market landscape - directly in NIBL's core industrial-bearing market.
- A significant decline in schedules from key OEMs in the textile and Radial Piston Pump segments, along with reduced demand from textile end-users, affected revenue in those segments - showing dependence on a small set of OEM schedules.
- While Industrial Gearboxes, Construction Machinery, Material Handling Equipment and Machine Tools performed in line with forecasts, Textile Machinery and Mining fell short of expectations; management notes market dynamics remain volatile and demand patterns continue to evolve.
- The overall business environment remained challenging within the industrial segment due to global economic uncertainty, rising geopolitical tensions, and disruptions caused by inter-country conflicts and policy shifts.
- The Company reports foreign exchange earnings of Rs. 2,300.31 lakhs and outgo of Rs. 586.79 lakhs for FY2025-26, and its growth mantra rests on entering new export markets such as the USA and South East Asian countries, so a material share of business is exposed to currency and cross-border trade conditions.
- Cost efficiency in the year came from stringent cost control in raw material and finished goods inventory; the energy annexure shows propane gas cost rose to Rs. 1,78,400 per ton from Rs. 69,800, and solar generation fell to 1,31,473 KWh from 3,19,879 KWh, leaving more of the load on purchased power.
- Based on paid-up equity share capital and net worth, the corporate governance provisions of SEBI LODR are not applicable to the Company; it provides a Corporate Governance report only on a voluntary basis. CSR provisions of Section 135 are likewise not applicable, and no CSR policy or activities exist.
